text: Then I lifted my eyes and looked, and there before me were four horns.
I asked the angel who was speaking with me, "What are these?" He answered me, "These are the horns that scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem."
Then the LORD showed me four craftsmen.

I asked, "What are these coming to do?" He said, "These are the horns that scattered Judah so completely that no one could lift his head. But these have come to terrify them, to cast down the horns of the nations that raised their horn against the land of Judah to scatter it."
Then I lifted my eyes and looked, and there before me was a man with a measuring line in his hand.
I asked, "Where are you going?" He said to me, "To measure Jerusalem, to see how wide and how long it is."
Then I saw the angel who was speaking with me going out, and another angel came out to meet him

versions.text: Then the angel who was speaking with me came forward, and another angel came out to meet him
versions.explanation: The Hebrew uses the same participle יֹצֵא for both angels; rendering the first as "came forward" obscures that parallel, and the attention-marker וְהִנֵּה ("behold/I saw") is dropped. Keeping "going out" preserves the parallel movement and the sense of the vision being observed.

text: and said to him, "Run, tell that young man: Jerusalem will be inhabited as a city without walls, because of the multitude of people and livestock within her.

versions.text: and said to him, "Run, tell that young man: Jerusalem will be settled as an open country, so many will be the people and livestock within her.
versions.explanation: "Settled as an open country" is awkward for oral reading, and "so many will be the people" blurs the causal force of מֵרֹב ("because of the multitude"). פְּרָזוֹת denotes unwalled settlements, so "a city without walls" is clearer and also prepares for the wall of fire in verse 9.

text: And I myself will be a wall of fire around her, declares the LORD, and I will be the glory within her."
"Up, up! Flee from the land of the north, declares the LORD, for I have scattered you to the four winds of heaven, declares the LORD.

versions.text: "Away, away! Flee from the land of the north, declares the LORD, for I have scattered you to the four winds of heaven, declares the LORD.
versions.explanation: הוֹי here is a summoning cry calling for attention and urgency; "Away, away!" overlaps with the following "Flee" and can be misread as dismissal. "Up, up!" keeps the rhythmic double interjection while letting the verb carry the idea of fleeing.

text: Up, Zion! Escape, you who dwell with the daughter of Babylon."

versions.text: Away, Zion! Escape, you who dwell with the daughter of Babylon."
versions.explanation: "Away, Zion!" can be heard as sending Zion away rather than as a summons to her; the same interjection as in verse 10 should be rendered consistently as an urgent call.

text: For this is what the LORD of hosts says: After his glory he sent me against the nations that plundered you—for whoever touches you touches the apple of his eye.
See, I will raise my hand against them, and they will become plunder for their own servants. Then you will know that the LORD of hosts has sent me.
Sing and rejoice, daughter of Zion! For I am coming, and I will dwell in your midst, declares the LORD.
Many nations will join themselves to the LORD on that day and become my people, and I will dwell in your midst. Then you will know that the LORD of hosts has sent me to you.
The LORD will take possession of Judah as his portion in the holy land, and he will again choose Jerusalem.
Be silent, all flesh, before the LORD, for he has roused himself from his holy dwelling.
